transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… I don’t know, my talking has gotten really messed up. Like I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. I’ll start trying to explain something simple, like an overnight shift at work, and then somehow I’m talking about soccer, and then paint colors, and then patient charts, and by the time I notice it, everyone’s looking at me like they’re lost.

It’s not even that I’m trying to change the subject. In my head it feels connected for a second, like one thing leads to the next, but when it comes out loud it’s like I skipped all the bridges between the thoughts. People ask me to slow down or repeat what I mean, and I try, but then I end up going somewhere else again. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I can see it happening while I’m talking sometimes, and I still can’t really pull it back.
Do you ever hear or see things that aren't there?

I don’t know… I mean, not like I’m seeing people standing in the room that nobody else sees, or hearing a clear voice talking to me, if that’s what you mean. I don’t think that’s happening.

Sometimes I second-guess myself, though, because when I’m tired or stressed, I’ll hear a noise and I’ll be like, “Was that someone saying something?” but then it’s just the hallway or somebody moving around. Or I’ll think I caught something out of the corner of my eye, but when I look there’s nothing weird there. I don’t know if that counts. It doesn’t feel like… a whole thing that isn’t there. More like I’m already on edge and my brain grabs onto stuff.

So, I guess my answer is no, not really. Not in a way I’m sure about.
Is this difficulty with keeping your thoughts in order when speaking happening in other areas of your life, like in your writing or when you're trying to organize tasks?

Yeah… I think it does, but the talking is the part people notice first. Like, when I’m trying to write something down, I’ll start with what I meant to say and then halfway through I’m suddenly adding details that don’t really belong there, or I can’t tell what order things should go in. It’s like the same problem as when I’m speaking.

At work, if I’m trying to explain an overnight shift or what happened with patient charts, I’ll begin in one place and then my mind jumps — soccer, colors on the walls, some random thing someone said — and in my head it feels like there was a connection, but when I say it or write it, it comes out all broken up. Then I look back and realize it doesn’t really make sense the way I thought it did.

Organizing tasks is kind of like that too. I can start doing one thing, then something reminds me of something else, and suddenly I’m off in another direction. But the worst is definitely when I’m trying to talk, because I can see people’s faces change, like they’re trying to follow me and they can’t. That’s what made me come in.
Do you find that your mood changes frequently or unexpectedly?

I don’t know if I’d say it changes a lot, like flipping back and forth all day. It’s more like… most days I wake up and I already feel heavy. Like before anything even happens, there’s this empty feeling sitting there, and I’m just carrying it around.

And then after work, after a shift, it can hit harder. I’ll get out to my car and just sit there, and sometimes I’m crying before I can even make myself drive home. It’s embarrassing to say because I’ll just be sitting in the parking lot trying to pull myself together, like I’m waiting for it to pass enough that I can actually turn the key and leave.

So I guess the mood doesn’t feel unexpected exactly. It’s just there most of the time, and sometimes it kind of caves in on me.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic, irritable, or unusually happy for several days or longer?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve had, like, several days where I was unusually happy or full of energy in a way that felt clearly different. I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m more wound up or more irritated, especially if I’m stressed or haven’t slept well, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as what you’re asking.

I wouldn’t say I suddenly become this really energetic person for days and days. If anything, I usually feel like I’m dragging myself through things. Sometimes I can get kind of restless or snappy, but it doesn’t feel like some big high mood or anything. It feels more like I’m tense, or overwhelmed, or I can’t settle.

So… I guess no, not that I can point to. But I’m not totally sure what counts, because I don’t always notice things clearly when I’m in the middle of them.
Have you ever felt abnormally happy or extremely energetic for more than a day?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re saying it, like abnormally happy or extremely energetic for more than a day. I’ve had times where I’ll feel a little more awake or kind of keyed up, but it usually doesn’t last, and it doesn’t feel like this big good mood or like I’m suddenly able to do everything.

Most of the time, if I’m energetic, it’s more like nervous energy, if that makes sense. Like I can’t sit still or I’m irritated, but not happy. I don’t remember having a stretch where people were like, “You’re acting unusually great,” or where I felt unstoppable or anything like that.

So… I’d say no, not really. Or at least not that I can clearly point to.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns lately?

I’m not totally sure what to say about “changes,” because my sleep has felt kind of all over the place in a way that I don’t always track very well. Like, I don’t keep a record or anything, so when someone asks me directly, I start second-guessing myself.

Some nights I feel like I’m lying there for a long time, just not really settled, and then other times I think I sleep but I still wake up feeling like I didn’t get much rest. But I don’t know if that’s new exactly, or if I’m only noticing it more because you’re asking. My schedule with work can make it hard to tell what’s a pattern and what’s just me being tired from the day.

So… I guess I’ve noticed that it doesn’t feel very consistent, but I can’t say clearly, like, “this changed on this day” or anything like that.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things in your daily life?

Yeah… I mean, I do worry, but I’m not sure how much is “often” compared to what’s normal. Like, I’ll get caught up thinking about regular things—work, whether I said something wrong, whether I forgot something, money stuff, just… basic life things—and sometimes it feels like my mind keeps circling around it longer than it should.

But I don’t know if I’d describe it as constant anxiety exactly. Some days it’s more in the background, like I’m tense and checking myself, and other days I’m just tired and don’t even have the energy to worry properly, if that makes sense. I guess I do have a hard time letting things go once they get in my head, even if the thing isn’t that big.

So… yes, I worry about daily things, probably more than I should, but I’m not sure how to measure it.
Have you ever had a period where you felt like you didn't need much sleep and still had a lot of energy?

I don’t think so… not like that, anyway. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep much, or I was up late and then had to go to work or do stuff the next day, but I wouldn’t say I had a lot of energy from it. Usually if I don’t sleep, I feel kind of worn down or foggy, even if I’m still moving around.

I guess sometimes I can push through because I have to, like if there are responsibilities or I’m already tense, but that doesn’t feel like not needing sleep. It feels more like I’m running on stress, if that makes sense. Like my body is awake but I don’t feel good or refreshed or unusually energetic.

So… no, I can’t really point to a period where I was sleeping very little and still felt energized or like I didn’t need it.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… yeah, definitely. That’s actually been one of the things I notice the most, even if I don’t always talk about it because it sounds kind of dramatic when I say it out loud.

I used to have stuff I cared about, like I used to sketch a lot—murals, mostly, or ideas for murals. I’d get really into the colors and the shapes and where something would go on a wall, even if it was just in a notebook and not a real project yet. And I used to like cooking for my friends, too. Not anything fancy all the time, but I liked making food and having people over, feeling like I was doing something good for them. And on weekends I’d play soccer sometimes, which used to help me feel like I was still part of things.

Now it’s like… I can remember that I liked those things, but I don’t feel the pull to do them. It all just feels pointless, or like too much effort for no reason. People message me and I’ll see it, and I know I should answer, and then I just don’t. I’ll leave it there and stay in my apartment instead. It’s not even always that I’m choosing to be alone in some big way—it’s more like everything feels flat, and I can’t make myself care enough to start.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being controlled or influenced by something outside of yourself?

Yeah… I mean, not exactly like somebody is moving my thoughts around like a remote control, if that’s what you mean. But I do feel like things are being… influenced, or like decisions around me are being made because of what people think is going on with me, even when they act like that’s not what it is.

At work, especially. I’m pretty sure my supervisors have changed my shifts around because they’re watching me and they think I might be unsafe or unstable or something. They’ll say it’s just staffing shortages, or somebody called out, or “we’re adjusting coverage,” but it doesn’t feel random. It feels too pointed. Like I’ll get moved off certain times or put somewhere different, and then I notice the cameras on the unit and I can’t stop thinking they’re checking to see what I’m doing, whether I’m acting normal, whether I’m a risk.

And people tell me, “That’s just how scheduling is,” or “The cameras are there for everybody,” and I understand that’s the explanation they give. I can repeat it back. But it doesn’t feel true to me. It feels like there’s another reason underneath it, and I’m the reason. Like they’re not saying it directly because they don’t want me to know, but I can tell by how the shifts change and how the supervisors look at me or don’t look at me.

So… I don’t know if that counts as my thoughts being controlled. But I do feel like something outside of me—my bosses, the cameras, the way the unit is set up—is influencing what happens around me and watching me, even when everyone keeps saying it’s not like that.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear when you were alone?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve heard, like, clear voices when I’m alone—like someone talking in the room or calling my name when nobody’s there. At least not in a way I could point to and say, “Yes, that definitely happened.”

Sometimes I hear noises and I’ll get stuck on them, like something in the hallway or the building settling or a phone buzzing somewhere, and I’ll stop and listen because I’m trying to figure out if it’s real. But I don’t know if other people would hear it or not, because usually I’m by myself when I notice it, so there isn’t anyone there to ask. And then if I check and nothing’s there, I just kind of tell myself maybe it was pipes or neighbors or something.

So… voices, no, not really. Sounds, maybe little things here and there, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Have you ever felt extremely irritable or angry for an extended period?

I don’t know if I’d call it “extremely” angry for a long time. I mean, I get irritated, sure. Like if people keep asking me questions or if something feels like it’s being handled in a stupid way, I can feel myself getting tense and short. But I don’t think I’ve had days and days where I’m just raging or ready to explode the whole time.

It’s more like… I get worn down, and then little things bother me more than they probably should. I might snap in my tone or get quiet because I’m trying not to say something I’ll regret. But extended anger, like staying furious for hours or days, I don’t really think so. Not that I’ve noticed. It’s not usually anger that sticks around like that for me.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Yeah… I think so. I haven’t really been weighing myself regularly, so I can’t give you an exact number, but my clothes are definitely looser. Like my work pants don’t sit the same, and I keep having to pull them up or tighten the belt more than I used to.

It’s mostly because I just don’t get hungry much anymore. I’ll go through a whole shift with just coffee, and then maybe I’ll grab crackers from the vending machine if I feel like I should eat something. Not even because I want them, more because I realize I haven’t eaten and I’m getting kind of empty-feeling. But actual appetite? It’s just not really there most days.

Sometimes I’ll think, “I should eat when I get home,” and then I just don’t, or I take a few bites and feel done. So yeah, I’d say my weight has probably gone down, even if I don’t know the exact amount.
Have you ever felt extremely happy or euphoric for several days in a row?

I don’t think so… not extremely happy, no. I mean, I’ve had good days, or maybe a few hours where I felt lighter because something went okay, like work wasn’t as bad or I got through something I was worried about. But euphoric for several days? Like unusually energized and happy in a way that keeps going? I don’t really recognize that in myself.

If anything, when I do feel better, I’m usually kind of cautious about it, like I don’t trust it to last. It’s not like I’m walking around on top of the world for days. I can laugh at something or feel relieved, but it doesn’t turn into this big stretch of feeling amazing. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had that.
Have you stopped enjoying activities that you used to like for more than two weeks?

Yeah. More than two weeks, definitely. It’s been… I don’t know, it feels like a while now. Things I used to actually care about just don’t pull me in anymore.

I used to sketch a lot, especially mural ideas. I’d fill pages with designs, like color blocks and outlines, and sometimes I’d get really caught up in it and lose track of time. Now I’ll see the sketchbook sitting there and it just feels like this dead object. Like I know I used to like it, I remember liking it, but I can’t really connect to that feeling.

And cooking, too. I used to cook for my friends sometimes, nothing fancy all the time, but I liked making food and having people over. Now when they text me, I usually just ignore it. Not because I hate them or anything, it just feels like too much effort and kind of pointless. Same with soccer on weekends. I used to go play, even if I was tired from work, but now I just stay in my apartment. I tell myself maybe next weekend, but then next weekend comes and I don’t go.

It’s like everything has the same flat feeling to it. I know those things used to matter to me, but right now they just don’t.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about things you've done or haven't done?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I feel bad about things, yeah, but I don’t know if I’d call it guilty exactly, or worthless. Those words feel kind of big.

Like, I’ll think about stuff I’m not doing — not calling people back, not keeping up with things, not being the way I’m supposed to be — and it sits on me. But it’s more like this heavy “I should be doing better” feeling than a specific thing I did wrong. Sometimes I’ll replay little things in my head, like something I said at work or how I handled something, and I’ll wonder if I made it worse or if people noticed I wasn’t right. But I don’t know if that’s guilt or just… being stuck thinking about it.

Worthless… I don’t know. I don’t usually say that word to myself directly. I guess there are times where I feel like I’m not much use to anybody, but it’s hard to tell if that’s the same thing you mean. It’s not like one clear thought all the time. It’s more just this low feeling, like I’m not doing enough and I’m letting things slip.
Have you ever thought about hurting yourself or wished you were dead?

Yeah… I have. I don’t like saying that out loud, but yes.

It’s usually after really bad nights, when I haven’t slept right or I’ve been lying there with my head just going and going. In the morning, or sometimes in the middle of the night, I’ll think… it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Not like I’m calmly deciding something, more like this thought drops in and it feels like everything is too heavy to keep carrying.

And sometimes it goes past that. Sometimes I do think, like, maybe I should just end it. Then I get scared because it feels too close, like it’s not just some random passing thought. When that happens, I usually tell someone. I don’t always want to, because it feels embarrassing and dramatic, but I get scared enough that I say something, because part of me doesn’t want to be alone with it.

So… yeah. I’ve wished I wouldn’t wake up, and I’ve had thoughts about ending it.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in most activities?

Yeah. Yes. It’s not just a bad day here and there. It’s been at least a couple weeks, honestly longer than that, where most days I wake up already feeling… heavy, I guess. Heavy and empty at the same time, if that makes sense.

It’s like before I even do anything wrong or anything happens, it’s already there when I open my eyes. I’ll just lie there for a minute and feel this weight in my chest and stomach, like the day is too much and I haven’t even started it yet. And it doesn’t really lift much. I can go through the motions, but it’s like I’m dragging myself through everything.

After work it gets really bad sometimes. I’ll finish a shift and get out to my car, and I won’t even be able to drive right away. I’ll just sit there in the parking lot crying, trying to get myself together enough to go home. It’s embarrassing because I keep thinking someone might see me, but I also can’t stop it right away. I just sit there feeling completely drained and hollow.

So, yeah… depressed, lost interest, all of that. It’s been most days, and definitely more than two weeks.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significant anxiety
doctor.question: Do you often feel anxious or worried about things in your daily life?

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about anxiety or general daily worry, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific anxiety/worry symptom. It should not be forced into another category like delusions or depression.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I do worry, but I’m not sure how much is “often” compared to what’s normal. Like, I’ll get caught up thinking about regular things—work, whether I said something wrong, whether I forgot something, money stuff, just… basic life things—and sometimes it feels like my mind keeps circling around it longer than it should.

But I don’t know if I’d describe it as constant anxiety exactly. Some days it’s more in the background, like I’m tense and checking myself, and other days I’m just tired and don’t even have the energy to worry properly, if that makes sense. I guess I do have a hard time letting things go once they get in my head, even if the thing isn’t that big.

So… yes, I worry about daily things, probably more than I should, but I’m not sure how to measure it.

inference.note: Added F32.9 and F41.9 due to patient's description of mood and anxiety symptoms

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of manic or hypomanic episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt like you didn't need much sleep and still had a lot of energy?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about a manic or hypomanic-type symptom—decreased need for sleep with high energy—which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not like that, anyway. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep much, or I was up late and then had to go to work or do stuff the next day, but I wouldn’t say I had a lot of energy from it. Usually if I don’t sleep, I feel kind of worn down or foggy, even if I’m still moving around.

I guess sometimes I can push through because I have to, like if there are responsibilities or I’m already tense, but that doesn’t feel like not needing sleep. It feels more like I’m running on stress, if that makes sense. Like my body is awake but I don’t feel good or refreshed or unusually energetic.

So… no, I can’t really point to a period where I was sleeping very little and still felt energized or like I didn’t need it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in activities
doctor.question: Have you noticed a decrease in interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to sketch murals, cook for my friends, and play soccer on weekends, but now all of that feels pointless and I usually just ignore messages and stay in my apartment.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about decreased interest or pleasure in things previously enjoyed, which matches Loss_of_Interest.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yeah, definitely. That’s actually been one of the things I notice the most, even if I don’t always talk about it because it sounds kind of dramatic when I say it out loud.

I used to have stuff I cared about, like I used to sketch a lot—murals, mostly, or ideas for murals. I’d get really into the colors and the shapes and where something would go on a wall, even if it was just in a notebook and not a real project yet. And I used to like cooking for my friends, too. Not anything fancy all the time, but I liked making food and having people over, feeling like I was doing something good for them. And on weekends I’d play soccer sometimes, which used to help me feel like I was still part of things.

Now it’s like… I can remember that I liked those things, but I don’t feel the pull to do them. It all just feels pointless, or like too much effort for no reason. People message me and I’ll see it, and I know I should answer, and then I just don’t. I’ll leave it there and stay in my apartment instead. It’s not even always that I’m choosing to be alone in some big way—it’s more like everything feels flat, and I can’t make myself care enough to start.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychotic symptoms
doctor.question: Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being controlled or influenced by something outside of yourself?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m sure the supervisors changed my shifts and watch me through the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe, even when people tell me it’s just staffing shortages.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about a psychotic belief that thoughts are being controlled or influenced by an outside force, which is most directly related to delusions.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, not exactly like somebody is moving my thoughts around like a remote control, if that’s what you mean. But I do feel like things are being… influenced, or like decisions around me are being made because of what people think is going on with me, even when they act like that’s not what it is.

At work, especially. I’m pretty sure my supervisors have changed my shifts around because they’re watching me and they think I might be unsafe or unstable or something. They’ll say it’s just staffing shortages, or somebody called out, or “we’re adjusting coverage,” but it doesn’t feel random. It feels too pointed. Like I’ll get moved off certain times or put somewhere different, and then I notice the cameras on the unit and I can’t stop thinking they’re checking to see what I’m doing, whether I’m acting normal, whether I’m a risk.

And people tell me, “That’s just how scheduling is,” or “The cameras are there for everybody,” and I understand that’s the explanation they give. I can repeat it back. But it doesn’t feel true to me. It feels like there’s another reason underneath it, and I’m the reason. Like they’re not saying it directly because they don’t want me to know, but I can tell by how the shifts change and how the supervisors look at me or don’t look at me.

So… I don’t know if that counts as my thoughts being controlled. But I do feel like something outside of me—my bosses, the cameras, the way the unit is set up—is influencing what happens around me and watching me, even when everyone keeps saying it’s not like that.

doctor.question: Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear when you were alone?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about auditory hallucinations, such as hearing voices or sounds others cannot hear, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific hallucination item or manifestation of hearing voices/sounds.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve heard, like, clear voices when I’m alone—like someone talking in the room or calling my name when nobody’s there. At least not in a way I could point to and say, “Yes, that definitely happened.”

Sometimes I hear noises and I’ll get stuck on them, like something in the hallway or the building settling or a phone buzzing somewhere, and I’ll stop and listen because I’m trying to figure out if it’s real. But I don’t know if other people would hear it or not, because usually I’m by myself when I notice it, so there isn’t anyone there to ask. And then if I check and nothing’s there, I just kind of tell myself maybe it was pipes or neighbors or something.

So… voices, no, not really. Sounds, maybe little things here and there, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of manic episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever felt extremely irritable or angry for an extended period?

target_item.reason: The question asks about prolonged irritability or anger, but the provided symptom profile does not include an item specifically covering irritability, anger, or manic/hypomanic mood symptoms.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call it “extremely” angry for a long time. I mean, I get irritated, sure. Like if people keep asking me questions or if something feels like it’s being handled in a stupid way, I can feel myself getting tense and short. But I don’t think I’ve had days and days where I’m just raging or ready to explode the whole time.

It’s more like… I get worn down, and then little things bother me more than they probably should. I might snap in my tone or get quiet because I’m trying not to say something I’ll regret. But extended anger, like staying furious for hours or days, I don’t really think so. Not that I’ve noticed. It’s not usually anger that sticks around like that for me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant weight change
doctor.question: Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: I barely get hungry anymore, so a lot of days I just drink coffee at work and maybe eat vending-machine crackers, and my clothes have gotten loose.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about recent significant changes in weight, which matches the weight/appetite change symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I haven’t really been weighing myself regularly, so I can’t give you an exact number, but my clothes are definitely looser. Like my work pants don’t sit the same, and I keep having to pull them up or tighten the belt more than I used to.

It’s mostly because I just don’t get hungry much anymore. I’ll go through a whole shift with just coffee, and then maybe I’ll grab crackers from the vending machine if I feel like I should eat something. Not even because I want them, more because I realize I haven’t eaten and I’m getting kind of empty-feeling. But actual appetite? It’s just not really there most days.

Sometimes I’ll think, “I should eat when I get home,” and then I just don’t, or I take a few bites and feel done. So yeah, I’d say my weight has probably gone down, even if I don’t know the exact amount.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of manic episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever felt extremely happy or euphoric for several days in a row?

target_item.reason: The question asks about an extended period of extremely happy or euphoric mood, which relates to manic or hypomanic symptoms; this symptom profile does not include a manic/euphoric mood item.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not extremely happy, no. I mean, I’ve had good days, or maybe a few hours where I felt lighter because something went okay, like work wasn’t as bad or I got through something I was worried about. But euphoric for several days? Like unusually energized and happy in a way that keeps going? I don’t really recognize that in myself.

If anything, when I do feel better, I’m usually kind of cautious about it, like I don’t trust it to last. It’s not like I’m walking around on top of the world for days. I can laugh at something or feel relieved, but it doesn’t turn into this big stretch of feeling amazing. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had that.

inference.note: F23 and F31.9 were ruled out due to lack of clear psychotic symptoms and manic episodes

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest in activities they once enjoyed for an extended period
doctor.question: Have you stopped enjoying activities that you used to like for more than two weeks?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to sketch murals, cook for my friends, and play soccer on weekends, but now all of that feels pointless and I usually just ignore messages and stay in my apartment.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of enjoyment or interest in previously liked activities lasting more than two weeks.

patient.answer:
Yeah. More than two weeks, definitely. It’s been… I don’t know, it feels like a while now. Things I used to actually care about just don’t pull me in anymore.

I used to sketch a lot, especially mural ideas. I’d fill pages with designs, like color blocks and outlines, and sometimes I’d get really caught up in it and lose track of time. Now I’ll see the sketchbook sitting there and it just feels like this dead object. Like I know I used to like it, I remember liking it, but I can’t really connect to that feeling.

And cooking, too. I used to cook for my friends sometimes, nothing fancy all the time, but I liked making food and having people over. Now when they text me, I usually just ignore it. Not because I hate them or anything, it just feels like too much effort and kind of pointless. Same with soccer on weekends. I used to go play, even if I was tired from work, but now I just stay in my apartment. I tell myself maybe next weekend, but then next weekend comes and I don’t go.

It’s like everything has the same flat feeling to it. I know those things used to matter to me, but right now they just don’t.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of persistent feelings of worthlessness or guilt
doctor.question: Do you often feel guilty or worthless about things you've done or haven't done?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about feelings of guilt or worthlessness, but the provided symptom profile does not include a distinct item covering excessive guilt or worthlessness.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I feel bad about things, yeah, but I don’t know if I’d call it guilty exactly, or worthless. Those words feel kind of big.

Like, I’ll think about stuff I’m not doing — not calling people back, not keeping up with things, not being the way I’m supposed to be — and it sits on me. But it’s more like this heavy “I should be doing better” feeling than a specific thing I did wrong. Sometimes I’ll replay little things in my head, like something I said at work or how I handled something, and I’ll wonder if I made it worse or if people noticed I wasn’t right. But I don’t know if that’s guilt or just… being stuck thinking about it.

Worthless… I don’t know. I don’t usually say that word to myself directly. I guess there are times where I feel like I’m not much use to anybody, but it’s hard to tell if that’s the same thing you mean. It’s not like one clear thought all the time. It’s more just this low feeling, like I’m not doing enough and I’m letting things slip.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of suicidal thoughts
doctor.question: Have you ever thought about hurting yourself or wished you were dead?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: After bad nights I keep thinking it would be easier if I didn’t wake up, and sometimes the thought comes that I should just end it, even though I get scared and tell someone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about suicidal thoughts, self-harm, or wishing to be dead.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I have. I don’t like saying that out loud, but yes.

It’s usually after really bad nights, when I haven’t slept right or I’ve been lying there with my head just going and going. In the morning, or sometimes in the middle of the night, I’ll think… it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Not like I’m calmly deciding something, more like this thought drops in and it feels like everything is too heavy to keep carrying.

And sometimes it goes past that. Sometimes I do think, like, maybe I should just end it. Then I get scared because it feels too close, like it’s not just some random passing thought. When that happens, I usually tell someone. I don’t always want to, because it feels embarrassing and dramatic, but I get scared enough that I say something, because part of me doesn’t want to be alone with it.

So… yeah. I’ve wished I wouldn’t wake up, and I’ve had thoughts about ending it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a major depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in most activities?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel heavy and empty from the time I wake up, and after shifts I’ll sit in my car crying before I can even drive home.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether there has been at least a two-week period of depressed mood or loss of interest, which is a major depressive episode screening question. The most direct item is depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah. Yes. It’s not just a bad day here and there. It’s been at least a couple weeks, honestly longer than that, where most days I wake up already feeling… heavy, I guess. Heavy and empty at the same time, if that makes sense.

It’s like before I even do anything wrong or anything happens, it’s already there when I open my eyes. I’ll just lie there for a minute and feel this weight in my chest and stomach, like the day is too much and I haven’t even started it yet. And it doesn’t really lift much. I can go through the motions, but it’s like I’m dragging myself through everything.

After work it gets really bad sometimes. I’ll finish a shift and get out to my car, and I won’t even be able to drive right away. I’ll just sit there in the parking lot crying, trying to get myself together enough to go home. It’s embarrassing because I keep thinking someone might see me, but I also can’t stop it right away. I just sit there feeling completely drained and hollow.

So, yeah… depressed, lost interest, all of that. It’s been most days, and definitely more than two weeks.

inference.note: Narrowed down from F41.9 due to patient's consistent reports of depressive symptoms and loss of interest in activities, which are more characteristic of a depressive disorder than an anxiety disorder.
